intro.title: The Common Grounds Media Matrix
intro.text: A smooth, slide-based presentation comparing the two countries. It charts shared seafaring history, culinary crossovers and language links, and also covers family, faith, dress, crafts, architecture, music, celebrations and people.

ui.hint: Swipe, scroll or use the arrow keys

slides.title: Hands that Create
slides.text: Villages became famous for crafts. Tunisia's Nabeul, Guellala in Djerba and Sejnane are known for pottery; Bahrain's A'ali has made pottery for over 4,000 years. Both countries weave wool, embroider with gold and silver thread, and make baskets from palm leaves.

captions.bahrain: Pottery of A'ali and the looms of Bani Jamra.
